title: Tailscale seemingly interferes with internet connectivity
body: ### What is the issue? Occasionally when Tailscale is enabled I lose the ability to reach the internet. It gets fixed after turning Tailscale off, so my first guess is something to do with the Tailscale config. This has happened to me on Android as well as MacOS Monterey. It is not clear what the trigger is because it does not happen all the time. For e.g. right now as I file this Tailscale is enabled: Is there anything I can do to debug this a little more? ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Are there any recent changes that introduced the issue? _No response_ ### OS macOS, Android ### OS version Monterey; Android 12 ### Tailscale version 1.34.1 (app store) ### Bug report BUG-d62ca7b2223acaa6f8def36043fc4ec13f9f2e0e0548594fc9727a72d78676dd-20230104081918Z-53c6c8975c5f5abb

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: If you disable "Use Tailscale Subnets" does the connection works as intended? If so, could it be that you have an advertised network in your tailscale network with the same network subnet as your current network?

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I have this issue as well and only with recent versions of tailscale. 

Internal network: 10.0.0.0/24 (does not overlap with any subnets we have on tailnet)
- Internet service independantly checked - no ping timeouts occurring when a device is directly attached to the internet service
- Other PCs that are connected to the same network hardware, that are not using tailscale are unaffected and don't have internet drop outs when ping is attempted against the same internet host that I test on my tailscale connected PC
- See 4 x 'Destination net unreachable' ping replies and then the ping responses resume working again
- Have tested two separate NICs in my PC, behaviour is present in both NICs
- The behaviour does not occur at all when the tailscale service is shut off on my PC
- We use magic DNS but only for an internal subnet which I don't believe is being used when I ping an internet service

Specs:
Windows 10 Pro 64-Bit 19045
NIC: Realtek Gaming 2.5GbE Family Controller and Realtek PCIe GbE Family Controller (two separate NICs, only one used at a time)
Tailscale version: 1.34.1 - I have seen this in the last couple of versions. 
It seems to be periodical - I have updated to version 1.34.2 and it isn't happening at the moment but I'll report back if it returns.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
I just found this issue since I did some testing today, after I wasn't able to do anything network related on my mobile connection.

Here is what I found, and I even have an idea about why it could happen to OP:

Pixel 6 Pro, latest security patches & update, official firmware. (= Android 13). Tailscale app up to date. 
When I switch networks (e.g. from WIFI to Mobile) tailscale get's disconnected. The device appears offline in my other nodes, but the app still thinks its active and android shows the key in the top bar to indicate an active vpn connection. Only after I reenable tailscale in the mobile network the phone successfully goes online in tailscale again. Same when I go from mobile to WIFI. 

Now my idea why it happens on the macbook too: Some routers are configured to broadcast both the 2.4Ghz 5Ghz network as one. In my home network I had to disable that because my macbook switched to 2.4Ghz all the time and kept using it, which caused me to surf like its 1999. But maybe @reporter has this configuration and macos does some kind of "network switch" too when switching between bands. 

@participant7 seeing that you have issues on android too: Did you try to re-enable tailscale after switching network? Do you see the same behaviour as me?

comments.body:
Just to throw another "Doh!" possible solution in there...   haven't had this problem at all until the last 3 days.  Today the frustration of not having internet and access to my tailscale network got too high and I began googling for potential solutions and ending up here as one of the threads looking into.

This thread gave me some good thoughts (thanks guys), so in trying some of the suggestions (none working), I got to the "turn off magic dns" option.  Turned off  tailscale so that I'd have internet, and logged into (web) tailscale via internet.   Before I even switched to the settings page, I noted something odd.

It said it hadn't seen my exit node machine in the last 3 days...   what????

Doh!   3 days ago I had taken that server down for maintenance, and now realize I don't think I brought it back up.    As a proper geek, I have quite a few servers in my home lab that I'll spin up, and I've setup 2 of them as exit nodes (1 for primarily use, and 1 as a backup), both servers that I usually leave up 24/7.

Sooooo, I quickly loaded back up tailscale (killing the internet connection), right clicked the tool-bar tailscale icon, and switched my exit node to my backup server (which was on).... and the skies parted and the sun shone   (errr I now have internet and tailscale simultaneously).

So for those who typically laugh at folks with the "is it plugged in" first tech support question...  double check you're not being the daily idiot.    (Hopefully my stint as today's idiot might help someone else, thus my admitting to all of this.  :)

comments.author: participant23
comments.body: Thanks everyone for the suggestions. I was having the same Internet issues. After reading these comments, I tried one other thing which resolved it for me on several of my devices, including an Apple TV. Btw, I didn't need to disable MagicDNS to make my devices work. While I was able to disable "Use Tailscale DNS settings" on my Mac through the app's settings, the Apple TV's app doesn't expose that same option in its settings UI, which led me to searching for another solution. Thankfully, the Tailscale web portal/dashboard does allow for the ability to disable the Tailscale DNS. 1. Go to https:///admin/dns 2. Scroll down to "Global nameservers". 3. You'll see a toggle to the right with a tooltip and text that says, "Override local DNS". Disable that. 4. Done. Hopefully your devices won't have issues connecting to the Internet anymore. Good luck! Btw, not sure if it's related to the cause of this issue, but I do use Pi-hole on my local network too.

comments.body:
This is an extremely generic issue that could be caused by a variety of reasons. In most of the cases here DNS seems involved, along with exit node misconfiguration, routes, bad interface switch detection, etc.

The comments here for the past 1.5 years have all been pointing at different causes, on different platforms, with different root causes. Most likely, some of the problems have probably been fixed in the meantime. All of this makes it hard to understand what this issue is actually tracking, so I'll be closing this.

If you experience a connectivity issue, please file a new issue **with a bug report identifier**. Or even better, please contact support. They can look at telemetry from your clients to understand what is actually going on.
